message.content:
Two related shared-hosting improvements from the Nxeon board. Work ONLY in `/opt/nxeon-wt-adminhost` (branch feature/adminhost). Commit + push when done. Do NOT run npm build/prisma — write code + `npx tsc --noEmit`. Match the site theme (navy/violet/cyan glass, Geist global) and reuse shared primitives (`components/ui/primitives.tsx`: PageHeader, .card, .btn-primary, .section-label, .table-shell, Badge, Field/inputs; admin components in `components/admin/`).

## Task 1 — Admin "Shared Hosting Plans" page is a mess; reorganize it (board card lvcrn0)
Find where hosting plans are managed in admin (start at `app/admin/hosting/page.tsx`, `components/admin/HostingInfra.tsx`, and any HostingPlan admin form; the model is `db.hostingPlan`). Redesign the hosting-plans admin UI to be clean and consistent with the OTHER admin plan pages (`app/admin/plans` for VPS, `app/admin/email-plans`, `app/admin/game-plans` — read those to match their layout/pattern): a tidy list/table of hosting plans with a clear create/edit form per plan. 
- Surface + make editable the plan's **storage/disk spec** and the other quotas (disk quota, websites, databases, bandwidth, mailboxes, price) — board card 349sjj notes the storage specs on shared-hosting plans need updating and shown clearly. Keep all fields DB-fed via `hostingPlan`; don't invent values.
- Keep it consistent with the VPS/email/game plan admin pages (same primitives, same form UX). Don't change pricing LOGIC — just the admin management UI + exposing the storage/quota fields.

## Task 2 — Show the first-month-free clearly on the hosting order/setup page (board card 20yrde "Update pricing")
On the customer shared-hosting order/setup UI (find it: `components/customer/HostingClient.tsx` and/or the hosting order flow) make the promo unmistakable: for each plan show **"FREE first month"** then **"renews at $X/mo"** (the real DB-fed plan price via the existing helpers). This is DISPLAY ONLY — do not change charge logic. First-month-free is HOSTING-ONLY (already gated by `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("HOSTING")`) — reflect that truthfully: FREE now, then the exact regular monthly price it renews at ("the price you sign up at is the price you renew at"). Prices DB-fed; displayed === charged.

## Hard rules
- No VAT/charge-logic changes. Prices strictly DB-fed (no hard-coded numbers). first-month-free stays hosting-only. No amber except semantic. tsc clean.
- Task 1 is admin-only (behind the existing admin guards); Task 2 is the customer hosting order page.

## Output
`npx tsc --noEmit` clean (report). Commit + push to origin/feature/adminhost. Report: the admin hosting-plans redesign (fields exposed, pattern matched), and the free-month display change on the customer hosting order page, confirming prices DB-fed + no charge-logic touched. Previews on staging.

NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)

You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.

Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.

Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).

Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.

Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.

Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.

A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

Done. Both tasks are implemented, `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean (exit 0), and the work is committed and pushed to `origin/feature/adminhost`.

## Task 1 — Admin shared-hosting plans redesign (board lvcrn0 / 349sjj)
The plans UI was a cramped 6-field create form + a stripped-down read-only table wedged into `HostingInfra.tsx`. It now matches the Email/Game plan admin pages exactly (card-per-plan with an inline "Edit" editor + a bottom "New plan" card).

- New `components/admin/HostingPlansAdmin.tsx` (server section) and `components/admin/HostingPlanControls.tsx` (client `HostingPlanForm` / `HostingPlanEditor` / `ToggleHostingPlanButton` / `DeleteHostingPlanButton`), mirroring `EmailPlanControls`.
- **All quotas now exposed + editable** (previously hidden or uneditable): storage/disk GB (rendered first and highlighted per 349sjj), websites, databases, bandwidth TB, mailboxes (−1 = unlimited), price, plus PHP versions, tagline, sort order, and the featured / free-migration flags. Each plan card shows the full spec sheet as chips.
- New server actions in `lib/actions-hosting.ts`: `adminSaveHostingPlan` (unified create+edit, all fields, slug-uniqueness excludes self, audit-logged), `adminDeleteHostingPlan` (refused while any account references the plan), `adminListHostingPlans` (full rows + account count). `adminListHostingInfra` trimmed to nodes-only; `HostingInfra` now renders nodes only. Kept `adminToggleHostingPlan`.
- Guard unchanged (`requireArea("fleet")`, matching the existing `/admin/hosting` page). No pricing logic touched — prices are stored/read-back only.

## Task 2 — First-month-free on the customer order page (board 20yrde)
`app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx` now resolves the promo server-side (`firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("HOSTING") && firstMonthFreeEnabled()`) and passes a `firstMonthFree` flag to `HostingClient`. When on:
- Each plan card shows **"Free first month"** then **"renews at $X/mo"** using the DB-fed `priceCents`.
- An emerald promo banner ("your first month is free… the price you sign up at is the price you renew at") and a per-selected-plan renewal note ("$0 today, then {plan} renews at $X/mo").

This is display-only — `orderHostingAccount` charge logic is untouched, prices are strictly DB-fed (`displayed === charged`), the promo stays hosting-only, and no amber/non-semantic colors were introduced (free/positive uses emerald).

Previews will be on staging. The branch has no PR yet — GitHub shows the create-PR link for `feature/adminhost`.
